title: Planet arrival: source-image orientation, pivots and composition audit
scope: Existing arrival sprites, all 55 V12/V14 profile source images, and 8 campaign globe sources. Read-only asset inspection; new calibration code only.

inspectionMethod.visual: All 55 ship profiles inspected: 47 V12 profiles on 4 labelled contact sheets composited onto an opaque dark background, 8 V14 profiles individually. All 8 globe sources on one sheet; 6 arrival sprites individually; 4 door fit composites compared.
inspectionMethod.pixel: Pillow and NumPy read native dimensions, alpha bounds and source hashes. A ship release contact is the last alpha > 128 pixel plus one at a manually selected underside column.
inspectionMethod.warning: Raw RGB in fully transparent pixels can contain coloured bands. Alpha inspection confirmed those pixels have alpha 0; they are not reported as visible source defects.
inspectionMethod.humanValidation: Not performed. Existing source human-validation/provenance contracts unchanged.

historicalBrowserCapturesInspected.meaning: Evidence of baseline composition only. These old captures do not attest the new implementation.

findings.subject: Carrier heading
findings.observed: The baseline moves the classic ship right while its forked prow points left. V12 and V14 sources for the same family may have opposite headings.
findings.correction: Resolve profile first; preserve native dimensions and calibrate individual forward axis before applying trajectory heading.
findings.status: calibration supplied; rendered fix must be verified separately

findings.subject: Flight capsule aspect and sockets
findings.observed: Baseline container is 2:1 while pod-flight is 1536x1024. object-fit:contain puts additional horizontal margins around the actual 3:2 image. A percentage of the container does not identify a source nozzle or nose.
findings.correction: Draw source with native aspect, then transform source-normalized nose, tail and effect origins through the same parent.

findings.subject: Atmospheric plasma origin and direction
findings.observed: The hot source head is near (100,505), not (0,362). The source wake axis is sloped from this point toward (1950,165), approximately -10.4 degrees. A horizontal flip alone neither aligns it to the source axis nor attaches it to the capsule.
findings.correction: Anchor the bow shock to the leading nose and rotate its measured source vector opposite projected velocity. Keep the wake behind the capsule body.

findings.subject: Ejection plume attachment
findings.observed: Release-jet is 1774x887 with origin near (280,500). Baseline releaseJet is an independent screen element with constant rotation and its own transform, not a child socket. Historical release capture shows plume below the pod rather than clearly opposite ejection.
findings.correction: Use the source emitter pivot and an explicit bay or pod socket with inherited scale/orientation; define the emitting owner so the effect cannot drift.

findings.subject: Hatch hinge and fit
findings.observed: Source depicts an upper hinge; manifest marks hinge-top. Baseline uses transform-origin:bottom left plus translation. Its contain box does not fit the ground opening.
findings.correction: Anchor pod hinge at (500,430), door hinge at (512,160), full door width ratio .8. Open around the fixed upper hinge; choose outward perspective rotation explicitly.
findings.status: source composite diagnostic compared four fits; final animation requires browser review

findings.subject: Ground contact
findings.observed: Source pod foot is (507.5,1496) on 1024x1536, but baseline anchors the outer canvas at 100%. contain adds more padding. Historical capture 14 shows visible pod-to-ground gap while hunter feet contact the line.
findings.correction: Use measured source foot and uniform world projection shared with contact effects.

findings.subject: Dust baseline
findings.observed: Impact dust ends near source y760/887; baseline uses a container at translate(-40%,-92%) and aspect-constrained contain. Its visible base can float above the contact line.
findings.correction: Use source foot (887,760), scale around that ground point, and assign foreground/background depth deliberately.

findings.subject: Opaque globe margins
findings.observed: All eight V10 planet plates are opaque 256x256 with black margins and off-centre disks. Border-radius:50% removes a rectangle but retains a broad black disk around the actual planet. This annulus is visible on historical carrier/release/descent captures.
findings.correction: Clip each measured ellipse rather than the full square; preserve the existing globe identity and dark limb.

findings.subject: Hatch shape conformity
findings.observed: The pointed leaf hatch and the rounded nearly rectangular cavity are not pixel-identical silhouettes. The .8 source-width fit reads better than .62 in static composites, but a transform is not a re-authoring of the panel.
findings.correction: Keep this as an artistic adaptation and inspect opening at game scale. Do not declare the sprite canonically reconstructed or human validated.

findings.subject: Strong perspective in some ship profiles
findings.observed: Some existing profiles are three-quarter views, especially Upgrade V14. Its historical profile contract requests nose-right, but the raster has pronounced perspective and multiple visible exhausts. Big Game is axis-symmetric; a unique bow cannot be read from that profile.
findings.correction: Preserve the source and clearly label authored-view or symmetric screen conventions. A 2D heading fix cannot certify a strict side or 3D reconstruction.
findings.status: explicit metadata limitations; no source identity substituted

limits: Calibration and source inspection are not human artistic validation.
No new claim about a canon docking bay: release points are cinematic underside contacts on the existing artwork.
Game Preserve V14 remains a rejected supplementary study; shipProfileAssetPath still resolves its existing V12 profile.
Current approved V14 identities and explicit project-original V12 identities preserve separate paths and calibrated axes.
Final motion, occlusion, pause/resume, reduced motion and responsive output belong to the new browser verification, not to this source report.
